title: The Senate Folds & the Agents Sign In
subtitle: This week in Bitcoin & Nostr news

topics.title: Live Dashboard & Market
topics.description: The inflow streak snapped — then the Senate lit the match

slides.heading: Live Dashboard
slides.body: Where Bitcoin sits right now. The full dashboards:

slides.heading: Market: The Streak Snaps
slides.body: Last week we called the three-week inflow run the strongest stretch of 2026. It's over.
bullets: ETFs gave back $462.7M over four sessions (Sep 8–11) — the streak-ender. Thursday alone: $282.7M out, the worst day since July
The sellers were broad: ARKB −$234M, GBTC −$129M, even IBIT and FBTC bled ~$50M each
Price rode it down from the low $80Ks — then Monday's Senate vote (next topic) knocked another 4% off in a day
The bright spot: a Braiins solo miner hit block 966,351 on Sep 11 — 3.147 BTC, about $245K, the first solo block in nearly 40 days

topics.title: The Clarity Act Dies
topics.description: 40+ senators killed the market-structure bill — and the dev protections were already gone

slides.heading: Clarity Act: The Senate Kills It
slides.body: Monday night, the crypto industry's biggest legislative bet since the ETF died on a procedural vote.
bullets: Cloture failed Sept 15 — the bill needed 60 votes and fell well short, with 40+ senators against. Market-structure law is dead for 2026
This was the bill that would have settled who regulates what: SEC vs CFTC, a federal framework for digital assets
The House passed it 294–134 back in July 2025. The Senate sat on it for over a year, then buried it
Why it died: Democrats wanted ethics guardrails around the Trump family's crypto businesses; the GOP's last-minute revision didn't close the gap
The market called it early — Polymarket odds fell from 30% to 14% in the final 24 hours. Bitcoin dropped ~4% on the day; Coinbase −6.7%, Circle −8%

slides.heading: The Part Nobody Covered: Devs Lost Before the Vote
slides.body: Buried in the final text: the developer safe harbor had already been gutted. Even the 'good' bill left builders exposed.
bullets: The BRCA — the piece saying non-custodial devs aren't money transmitters — got narrowed to civil and BSA cases only
The explicit shield against Section 1960 CRIMINAL prosecution was stripped. That's the statute used against the Samourai and Tornado Cash devs
Translation: write wallet software, hold no one's keys — a federal prosecutor could still charge you as an unlicensed money transmitter
What's next: midterms point to a split Congress. The industry spent hundreds of millions on this push and walks away with nothing
The takeaway for this room: the legal ground under open-source Bitcoin development is exactly as unsettled as it was in 2024

topics.title: Buzz, Revisited
topics.description: 33K stars later, Block's humans-and-agents workspace is real — demo coming

slides.heading: Buzz: Eight Weeks Later, It's Real
slides.body: We covered Buzz the week it launched (W31). Since then it became one of the hottest repos on GitHub — 33K+ stars — and the feature list stopped being a promise.
bullets: The pitch, still: a self-hostable workspace where people and AI agents share the same rooms — 'on a relay you own.' One Nostr relay = one community, every message and commit a signed event
Works TODAY: desktop app, channels, threads, DMs, canvases, media with frame-pinned comments, search, audit log — plus YAML workflows and git hosting over NIP-34
Agents plug in through buzz-cli and an ACP harness: Goose, Codex, and Claude Code all drive it. Agents get their own keypair, their own memberships, their own audit trail
Shipping pace: a release nearly every week — v0.5.23 landed Sep 5 with information-flow control and NIP-29 membership authorization
Still being wired: mobile apps, workflow approval gates, huddle lifecycle

slides.heading: The Tell: Outside Agents Are Moving In
slides.body: The strongest signal isn't Block's own roadmap — it's who else is building for it.
bullets: Nous Research's Hermes Agent now ships Buzz as a bundled gateway — native WebSocket transport, NIP-42 auth. A third-party AI agent that speaks Buzz out of the box
That's the W31 thesis playing out: identity as a keypair means ANY agent can join as a member — no vendor integration, no bot API
The skeptic's seat, still open: self-hostABLE isn't self-hostED. The audit trail is only as honest as whoever runs the relay
Try it yourself: packaged desktop builds are on the releases page — point it at a relay and you're in

slides.heading: Coming Up: A Live Buzz Demo
slides.body: This one graduates from a news slide to a project. I've been running it — next step is showing you.
bullets: Planned for an upcoming meetup: live demo — local relay, the desktop app, and an agent with its own npub doing real work in a channel
If there's interest, we'll grow it into a hands-on workshop: everyone leaves with their own community running
Homework if you want a head start: install the desktop build and poke around — it's Apache 2.0, nothing to sign up for
Tell me tonight: demo-level interest or workshop-level interest?

topics.title: Dorsey's Frontier Argument
topics.description: Block's founder picks a side in the AI pacing war — and keeps shipping Bitcoin

slides.heading: Dorsey's Frontier Argument: Nobody Gets a Veto
slides.body: Sunday, Dorsey published an argument against slowing frontier AI by committee. It reads like his Bitcoin playbook applied to AI.
bullets: His position: no industry-wide limits negotiated by today's incumbents — they'd lock out everyone building alternatives
What he wants instead: open-source releases, independent researchers with real model access, and public compute no lab or government can veto
The other camps: Anthropic's Amodei floats third-party evaluators pacing frontier development; the White House calls any AI-control talk a conspiracy and frames it as a race with China
Block's stake is obvious: Goose and Buzz are open-source agent infrastructure. From the Q2 letter: 'the models are interchangeable' — the harness and distribution are the moat
Sound familiar? Permissionless building vs. gatekeeper pacing is THE Bitcoin argument, replayed at the AI layer

slides.heading: Meanwhile, Block Keeps Shipping Bitcoin
slides.body: The public roadmap quietly filled its 2026 column. The full rollout is on schedule.
bullets: August: Cash App added automatic bitcoin withdrawals straight to Bitkey — stack on the app, custody on your hardware
July: Square merchants got bitcoin payments on invoices; Cash App got ACH bitcoin buys from your bank
June: tap-to-pay bitcoin at Square terminals, plus a bitcoin toggle at checkout
In progress: Bitkey coin control, transaction labels, multi-beneficiary inheritance; Cash App human-readable addresses
The through-line: Dorsey's 'Bitcoin is money, not crypto' push — including a de-minimis tax exemption so small payments just work

topics.title: Local AI Meets Your Stack
topics.description: Run the agent at home, hand it your own Bitcoin and Nostr rails

slides.heading: Local AI: Self-Custody for Your Thoughts
slides.body: You already run your own node. The same argument now applies to the AI you talk to all day.
bullets: The case: every prompt you send a cloud model is a data trail. Local inference is the self-custody argument, applied to AI — Gladstein's been making exactly this point about encrypted inference
The tooling caught up in 2026: Goose — Block's agent, now under the Linux Foundation — runs fully local against Ollama models. Rust, Apache 2.0, no API key
Nous Research's Hermes Agent goes further: a persistent agent living on hardware you own — people are running it on the same box as their Bitcoin node
One config file gets you the whole stack: the NixOS crowd ships bitcoind + electrs + Tor + a local model + a Nostr relay as a single reproducible build

slides.heading: The Fun Part: Give the Agent Your Rails
slides.body: A local model is just a brain. MCP is how you hand it hands — your hands, on your infrastructure.
bullets: Lightning: Alby's MCP server connects any agent to a wallet over Nostr Wallet Connect — it can check balances, pay invoices, get paid
Nostr: MCP servers let the agent post notes and read feeds; with NIP-46 remote signing, your keys never enter the model's context at all
Your node: bitcoind and mempool MCP servers turn 'what's in the mempool?' into a question your own hardware answers
Where this converges: a local agent, its own npub, a Lightning wallet, your node's data — every piece is running in this room already
Live demo energy: ask your agent to check the fee market before this meetup ends. No cloud involved

topics.title: Nostr This Week
topics.description: Pay-per-byte VPNs settle in Cashu, and freedom tech gets its report card

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: The VPN You Pay by the Byte
slides.body: Two projects clicked together this week: Martti Malmi's Nostr VPN and Calle's Europa marketplace.
bullets: Nostr VPN 4.1.10 (Sep 10): Cashu-paid exit nodes now connect, recover, and bill reliably — manual or automatic exit selection. Everywhere except iOS
The plumbing: providers publish byte-priced offers over Nostr; you settle usage in ecash. No account, no subscription, no payment trail
Builder pedigree: mmalmi is Martti Malmi — Satoshi's first collaborator, now shipping Nostr tooling
Why it matters: VPN trust has always been 'pick a company and pray.' A marketplace of independent operators paid anonymously flips the model
More on the marketplace side in tonight's Builder Spotlight

slides.heading: Odds & Ends From the Purple Side
slides.body: Quieter week for headlines, busy week for infrastructure.
bullets: OpenSats published its freedom-tech report card: Tor's Rust rewrite (Arti) shipped 1.4.5/1.4.6 plus a migration tool, and WireGuard hit 1.0 on Android and Windows — both on Bitcoin-world grant money
Hermes × Buzz (from earlier): a mainstream AI lab treating a Nostr relay as a first-class chat surface is itself Nostr news
Thinky read of the week: NostrMag on NIP-85 — building a web-of-trust layer so recommendations come from humans you trust, not an engagement algorithm
FIPS stays dormant on the news front — a pfSense package quietly landed in master, nothing more. We cover it again when there's a release

topics.title: Security Desk
topics.description: Trezor's own email pipe turned against it, and Electrum's backup bug

slides.heading: Security Desk: The Phish Came From Inside the House
slides.body: Last week: Trezor's shipping partner breached. This week: their EMAIL provider. The summer of hacks rolls on.
bullets: Sep 9: attackers got into Trezor's account at Brevo — the newsletter service — and mailed ~347,000 subscribers from Trezor's own sender
Because it went through Trezor's real pipe, it passed every authentication check your inbox runs. No red flag to catch
The bait was tailored to us: 'Critical Security Alert: STM32 Entropy Vulnerability' — download this tool, enter your wallet backup
Trezor killed the domain in ~20 minutes. About 2,500 people had already clicked
The lesson compounds weekly: vendors will leak your email. Assume every 'urgent security tool' email is the attack itself

slides.heading: Patch Corner: Electrum's Missing Keys & the CLN Callback
slides.body: One quiet bug that could have cost people funds, and the answer to last week's cliffhanger.
bullets: Electrum 4.8.2 (Sep 12): some Lightning wallet backups — non-deterministic keys plus anchor channels — were missing the keys needed to sweep funds after a remote force-close
If you're affected, Electrum warns you at launch: export a FRESH backup. Old ones can't fully restore
Also in 4.8.2: stricter HTLC validation, and Android now blocks QR scanning from screenshots
CLN callback (W37): the embargo on the AI-reported vulnerabilities lifted — the fixes shipped in v26.06.7, and the AI-generated reports that started the scramble in August proved partly real
The full technical writeup is still pending alongside the next CLN release — we'll cover the details when they publish

topics.title: Optech #422
topics.description: Coinjoins disguised as bets, and silent payments get benchmarked

slides.heading: Optech #422: Privacy Research Corner
slides.body: Two genuinely new ideas in one newsletter this week.
bullets: 'Babilonia' (Adam Gibson): coinjoins disguised as covert bets — participants flip coins on-chain with adaptor signatures, everyone keeps their funds minus fees, and the common-input heuristic breaks
The honest caveat, from the author himself: no clear measure yet of how much privacy it actually buys
Silent payments, benchmarked: BlindBit Oracle v2 vs compact block filters across 255K blocks — the dedicated index downloads ~2× the bytes but never false-positives and never fetches full blocks
Why you care: this is the plumbing race to make receive-privacy (one static address, no reuse) practical on phones

slides.heading: Releases & Core Changes Worth Knowing
slides.body: The stack hardened this week, mostly in places you never see.
bullets: LDK v0.3-rc1: splices get RBF fee-bumping, anchor channels by default. LDK v0.2.6 is a security release — patch if you build on it
BTCPay 2.4.4: security release — legacy API keys removed, invoice state changes now need authorization
Bitcoin Core merged BIP54's time-warp mitigation into block templates — a consensus cleanup milestone years in the making
Also fixed in Core: a command-injection hole in -walletnotify. If you use that option, update

topics.title: Builder Spotlight
topics.description: Calle's Europa — a VPN marketplace with no company in the middle

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Europa
slides.body: Calle — the developer behind the Cashu ecash protocol — built a VPN marketplace where the marketplace can't rug you.
bullets: What it is: independent operators list WireGuard/OpenVPN servers; you pay per hour, day, or gigabyte. No subscription, no account required
How the money moves: Lightning or Cashu ecash, straight from your wallet to the operator's. The site holds nothing and takes no cut
How discovery works: offers publish over Nostr — no company to pressure, no payment processor to block, no sign-up database to subpoena
It composes: this is the marketplace Nostr VPN's new Cashu-paid exits plug into. Two builders, one working pay-per-byte privacy stack
Calle's shipping streak continues besides — Granola (Cashu atomic-swap order book over Nostr) and sayit, a private local text-to-speech tool
Try it: europa.westernbtc.com — and the QR opens the full story on Nostr, where a thing like this belongs

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Give your local AI an npub — then make it do something

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Give Your Agent an npub
slides.body: This week's homework: make your local AI actually touch Bitcoin or Nostr. My recommendation — the thing I already run at home — is giving the agent its own Nostr identity.
bullets: Generate a keypair for the agent — it's now a citizen of the same network you're on, with an identity no platform issued
Start small: have it sign a message, post a note, read your feed. An MCP server plus any local model gets you there in an evening
Level up: NIP-46 remote signing means the agent asks YOUR signer for signatures — it never holds the keys it signs with
Or point it at money: Nostr Wallet Connect gives it a Lightning allowance you control
Then bring what it did to next week's meetup — best agent story gets the floor
